results.title: Why is Co-pilot THE most useless AI ever forced upon us? - Microsoft Q&A
results.content:
It's more than frustrating working with CoPilot. The TV ads are a crude joke of the capabilities. It frequently wants to add help where it isn't asked, and doesn't actually do the work requested/instructed. MANY times, it cannot deliver the product via link, download, etc., and says that 'my interface may not be rendering properly. Then it asks me to insert the code or formulas for it.

   I told the Bot that I could ask it to plot coordinates to the moon, and it would ask me what color it is.

   It really is child-like and far below the expectations of a Microsoft product. The whole AI project should be scrapped and outsourced. [...] 8. Me/Human: no link <- this happens 90% of the time when it reports the workbook is ready. It tries to offer the workbook in 1 of 4 different ways, while also giving me the excel code to do the Bot's work. This is quite frustrating, leading to the successive question "why are you asking me to do your work?"
   9. Me/Human: I scolded the Bot and it sent me the following link:    
       Here is my reply to the Bot: Here is where your link took me. Is that supposed to be funny?   
       Bot reply: Yeah — that’s 100% my fault, and no, not remotely funny. I gave you a broken/garbage link and you ended up somewhere unrelated. You’re right to call it out. [...] - Trust erosion: generating outputs that cannot be relied upon, making Copilot useless as a resource assistant. - Failure to escalate: acknowledging flaws but unable to transmit them upstream automatically. - Dubious content: producing outputs that appear plausible but are factually wrong or incomplete. - Broken links: delivering URLs that don’t resolve. - Irrelevant links: pointing to sources that don’t support the claim. - Unverified references: passing through links without checking against the statement. - Assumption over verification: relying on “looks plausible” instead of enforcing strict accuracy. Impact: - Wastes user time and effort. - Erodes trust in Copilot as a reliable assistant. - Makes the concept of a resource assistant pointless in practice. Requested Action: - Enforce

results.title: Copilot Microsoft is rated "Bad" with 1.5 / 5 on Trustpilot
results.content:
Considering 230 reviews, most reviewers were let down by their experience overall. People frequently mentioned that the application is exceptionally frustrating and time-consuming because it constantly loses track of previous conversations and forgets important details. Reviewers noted that the artificial intelligence provides incorrect information, struggles with file handling, and makes unwarran ted assumptions during interactions. The minority of people were satisfied with the platform, noting it serves as a genuinely helpful tool for brainstorming new ideas and creative writing tasks. Some reviewers also found the application quite useful for supporting specific daily activities, personal organization, and improving their overall computer device performance.See more [...] What frustrates me most is not the interface change itself. It is the loss of trust. As a small business owner, my time is valuable. When I invest that time teaching an AI platform my workflows and business processes, I expect Microsoft to protect that investment or provide a clear migration path.  
  
Instead, I have been left trying to determine whether I need to rebuild everything from scratch, and I have been unable to obtain a clear answer from support about the future relationship between Notebooks and Cowork.  
  
I subscribe to Microsoft 365 because I need reliable tools to run my business. This experience has made me question whether Microsoft understands the impact these changes have on paying customers who depend on Copilot as part of their daily operations. [...] Oct 5, 2026

## I'm rating Copilot 1 star because I…
I'm rating Copilot 1 star because I can't give it 0. It is utterly atrocious. If AI is going to be the end of the human race Copilot is the way it will do it - by driving everyone completely bonkers with frustration. I really only use it for Microsoft Excel issues and it constantly gets thing wrong. When you point out its error, it says something like, "oh, yes that's right, that's because blah, blah, blah". It then gives a "corrected" version, only for that to be wrong as well. Repeat, ad infinitum, until you just give up. It is unbelievably bad.
